methodology: Named earned-degree holders found by reviewing each school’s notable-alumni material and the relevant official award or office records. Count a person once per school and category. Include all genders and historical school names; exclude honorary-only degrees, attendance without an earned degree, nominees, finalists, members of a winning team or film without an individual award, and executives without the qualifying CEO title and year overlap. The one team exception is a Pulitzer Prize awarded to a newsroom’s staff: a graduate a source names as part of that staff counts. A degree type such as B.A. is shown only where a cited source states it; otherwise the entry gives the class year. These are verified named graduates in the reviewed sources, not a claim of complete all-time coverage.

categories.name: Nobel Prize winners
categories.definition: Named Nobel laureates who earned a DePauw or Wabash degree.

depauw.notes: Reviewed DePauw's 100 CLAS Alumni roster, notable alumni and Nobel laureate records. Ferid Murad is the verified graduate; Nobel laureates listed as lecture guests or unrelated alumni are excluded.

wabash.notes: Reviewed Wabash alumni materials and Nobel laureate records. No Wabash graduate qualifying in the reviewed records; visitors and unrelated Nobel recipients are excluded.

categories.name: U.S. vice presidents
categories.definition: People who served as Vice President of the United States and earned a degree from either school.

depauw.notes: Reviewed DePauw alumni and federal biographies. Dan Quayle graduated in 1969.

wabash.notes: Reviewed Wabash alumni and federal biographies. Thomas R. Marshall graduated in 1873.

McDonald, Newton Booth, James Watson, Elmer Thomas, Daniel Voorhees, and Dan Quayle. State legislators alone are excluded.

categories.name: Fortune 500 CEOs
categories.definition: People who served as chief executive officer of a company on the U.S. Fortune 500 during an overlapping ranking year; subsidiaries and chair-only roles do not qualify.

depauw.notes: Reviewed named DePauw business leaders in College records against company leadership biographies, SEC filings, and dated U.S. Fortune 500 lists (for 1996, 1997, 2000 and 2008 the full lists as CNN Money published them, in Internet Archive copies). Each displayed graduate has a sourced CEO tenure and at least one matching Fortune ranking year; chair-only roles are excluded. Richard D. Wood earned his degree at Purdue, Judson Green led a Disney division rather than the company, and Robert R. Frederick (RCA, 1985 to 1986) is not shown because no dated Fortune ranking for RCA could be checked.

wabash.notes: Reviewed named Wabash business leaders against school class records, company biographies, SEC filings, historical U.S. Fortune 500 lists, and the Congressional Research Service 1983 executive directory. Robert E. Allen, W. Paul Tippett, and Walter Y. Elisha have sourced CEO service and an overlapping rank; Allen’s tenure ends in 1997, when AT&T’s proxy statement says his successor became CEO. James L. Keyes is excluded: he is not the Johnson Controls CEO James H. Keyes. John Bachmann is excluded: Jones Financial is on none of the Fortune 500 lists reviewed for his years as managing partner.

categories.name: Rhodes Scholars
categories.definition: Named Rhodes Scholarship awardees who earned a degree from either college; finalists do not qualify.

depauw.notes: Reviewed the official Rhodes House award records returned for DePauw and traced earned-degree evidence for the named graduates. Three degree-holders are supported in the reviewed sources: Douglas Hallward-Driemeier (1989), John McNaughton (1948 award; DePauw 1942), and Robert Montgomery Stephenson (1916 award; A.B. 1913). The Rhodes Trust’s table of winners by institution also counts three for DePauw. Carlton Long (class of 1983) transferred and won his scholarship at Columbia, so he is not counted.

The Rhodes Trust’s table of winners by institution also counts nine for Wabash. For five of the nine (Pifer, Osborne, Littell, Barnett and Burnett) the cited page gives a class year only; no page that states the degree has been found yet.
